package_info.package_name: Smart Scale (AEG PW 5653 BT / VScale / com.vtrump.vscale)
package_info.package_manager: Android/iOS App Store (mobile app), Embedded BLE firmware
package_info.why_malicious: The smart scale and its companion apps collect and transmit excessive private user/device data to third-party servers (often in China) without user consent or encryption, request dangerous permissions, and expose users to hardware denial-of-service and privacy attacks via insecure BLE characteristics and unencrypted network traffic.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During standby, the code writes a value to the Immediate Alert characteristic, causing the device to crash and become unresponsive until power-cycled.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This write operation causes a persistent denial-of-service, requiring physical intervention to recover.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal BLE alert characteristics should not allow remote crashing of the device.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Alert characteristics are used for proximity alerts, not device control.
key_indicators: Device crash on specific BLE write

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code writes to the privacy flag, allowing tracking of the device by keeping the MAC address fixed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allows persistent tracking of users by disabling BLE privacy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Privacy should be enabled by default and not writable by arbitrary clients.
key_indicators: Fixed MAC address in BLE advertisements

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code changes the device name to a custom value, which can be used for social engineering or device identification.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allows attacker to rename device for phishing or confusion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Device name should not be arbitrarily writable.

execution_context.code_behavior: At runtime, the app downloads APK files from remote servers and saves them to external storage, potentially enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and saving APKs from remote sources can lead to silent malware installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should not download or install arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: App update mechanisms (should be signed and verified).

snippet_5.code_behavior: At runtime, the app collects device identifiers, network info, and user data, then sends it unencrypted to third-party servers in China.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive user/device data is exfiltrated without encryption or user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should not collect or transmit this level of private information.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry (should be opt-in, anonymized, and encrypted).
key_indicators: Unencrypted transmission of IMEI, MAC, SSID
Data sent to third-party analytics in China

snippet_6.code_behavior: At install-time, the app requests excessive permissions, including filesystem and location access, not justified by its functionality.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Over-privileged apps increase attack surface and privacy risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should not need location or filesystem mount permissions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fitness apps with mapping features (not relevant here).
